newsitem.title: INDIA: Four of 10 Indians in poverty, newspaper says.
newsitem.headline: Four of 10 Indians in poverty, newspaper says.

text.p: A government agency estimates four of every 10 Indians live in poverty, the Times of India said on Sunday, citing a new study that could add more than 200 million people to the poverty rolls.

The revision has potentially important implications as Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's centre-left coalition has pledged to provide cereals to those living below the poverty line at half the market price.

The revised estimate also suggests that free-market policies launched by former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in 1991 and endorsed by Deve Gowda have not brought down the incidence of poverty. The daily said the Planning Commission estimated 40 percent of India's estimated 930 million people -- or some 370 million -- lived below the poverty line in the 1994/95 fiscal year that ended on March 31, 1995.
An earlier official estimate put the share at 16.6 percent.

The commission based the revised estimate on a new methodology, recommended by an expert committee, that takes into account variations in the incidences of poverty among states and between rural and urban areas, the newspaper said.
"The committee's method yields an estimate closer to ground reality," the newspaper quoted Planning Commission deputy chairman Madhu Dandavate as saying.

Planning Commission officials could not be reached for comment. A Finance Ministry official said the commission's estimate had not yet been endorsed by the cabinet and thus remained an unofficial calculation.

Under the new estimate, some 370 million Indians live below the poverty line, defined as 264 rupees ($7.40) in household consumption per urban dweller each month. The amount drops to 228 rupees ($6.40) in rural areas.
